panel.api.accessMissing: Set “access” (a list of inbounds) or “kind” and “on”.
panel.api.awgDocMissing: The “doc” field is required — the contents of the export file.
panel.api.backupNothing: Nothing to save: all parts are excluded.
panel.api.backupParts: “{field}” must be a list of parts: {list}.
panel.api.badPort: “{field}” must be a port number, an integer from 1 to 65535.
panel.api.badMtuAction: “action” must be reissue, s4 or keep.
panel.api.badTtl: “ttl” must be a number of seconds.
panel.api.dupExit: This pool row duplicates the key in the row above: the gateway doesn’t use it, and it has no settings of its own. Rename or turn off the original exit, and delete the extra row from the “Telegram API proxy” pool.
panel.api.fieldBool: Field “{field}” must be true or false.
panel.api.fieldKinds: Field “{field}” must be a list of inbounds, for example {example}.
panel.api.githubKeyString: The GitHub key must be a string (“token”).
panel.api.hostMissing: Set the address (“host”) or ask to detect it (“detect”: true).
panel.api.hy2Nothing: Nothing to change: «hop» or «cert» is needed.
panel.api.keyTooLong: The key is longer than {kb} KB — this is not an exit key.
panel.api.loginStrings: Login and password must be strings.
panel.api.newPasswordString: The new password must be a string (“password”).
panel.api.noPassword: No panel password is set: sign in with a one-time link (gokaskad menu → 18 → 1, or the bot) or set a password (gokaskad menu → 18 → 2).
panel.api.oldEngine: Forwards use the old forwarding engine (iptables), but the panel manages only nftables forwards (gokaskad menu → “Forwarding engine and migration”).
panel.api.pasteKey: Paste a VPN key (vless, hy2, ss, trojan, vmess, vpn://) or the whole text of an AmneziaWG .conf file.
panel.api.publicNeedsPassword: Set a panel password first: with access from the internet you sign in only with the password or a one-time link, and the SSH tunnel asks for the password too.
panel.api.routeMissing: No route given (“via”: pool, group:<group id>, exit:<exit id>, direct or block).
panel.api.stale: No fresh data from the collector (kaskad-gw-collect): the state of protocols and exits, sessions and counters are unknown.
panel.api.subUrlTooLong: The subscription link is longer than {max} characters.
panel.api.tooManyTabs: Too many panel tabs are open (more than {max}): this one updates by polling — close the extra ones.
panel.auth.kdfBusy: The panel is busy checking other sign-ins — try again in a minute.
panel.auth.loginFormat: login: 1–32 characters — Latin letters, digits, dot, hyphen, underscore
panel.auth.passwordNotString: the password must be a string
panel.auth.passwordSpaces: password: no leading or trailing spaces and no control characters
panel.auth.tooManyTries: Too many sign-in attempts from this address. Try again in {min} min.
panel.cli.helpDomain: domain on which nginx serves the panel ("" — remove)
panel.cli.helpForce: take the port even if it’s in use
panel.cli.helpGenerate: generate a password and show it once
panel.cli.helpInstall: install and start the panel service
panel.cli.helpLogin: login (default: the current one or admin)
panel.cli.helpPath: secret path (default: the current one or a new app-<86 characters>)
panel.cli.helpProxy: listener for nginx: the panel on a domain at a secret path
panel.cli.helpPublic: Access from the internet: HTTPS on the external address
panel.cli.helpPurge: also remove the panel password and settings
panel.cli.helpRefresh: rewrite the unit only if it differs
panel.cli.helpRemove: stop and remove the panel service
panel.cli.helpRequirePassword: require the password in the SSH tunnel too
panel.cli.helpServe: the panel server (run by the service)
panel.cli.helpUnit: update the installed service unit without a restart
panel.cli.hostingFirewall: If your hosting provider has its own firewall, open port {port}/tcp in it.
panel.cli.installNoPassword: No password set: the tunnel doesn’t need one; set one for access from the internet ({menu}).
panel.cli.installRunning: The panel is running: {url} (via an SSH tunnel).
panel.cli.linkHead: One-time sign-in link (valid for {min} min, single use):
panel.cli.linkTunnel: Open it after starting the SSH tunnel: {cmd}
panel.cli.notRunning: The panel isn’t running: the setting takes effect when it starts.
panel.cli.passwordDone: Panel password set (login {login}). Sessions with the old password are closed.
panel.cli.passwordFromStdin: The password is read from stdin: {cmd}
panel.cli.passwordSaveIt: Save it: it won’t be shown anywhere again.
panel.cli.proxyNoDomain: Domain: not set — only the names 127.0.0.1/localhost are allowed
panel.cli.proxyNoPassword: No password set: via nginx you can sign in only with a one-time link; set a password in {menu}.
panel.cli.proxyOn: Listener for nginx is on: unix:{sock} (no tunnel sign-in here — password or link only).
panel.cli.publicNoPassword: No password set: for now you can sign in only with a one-time link; set a password in {menu}.
panel.cli.publicOffDone: Access from the internet is off: the panel is reachable only via an SSH tunnel ({cmd}).
panel.cli.publicSelfSigned: The browser will warn about a self-signed certificate: check the fingerprint and continue.
panel.cli.publicSignIn: Sign in with the password or a one-time link ({menu}).
panel.cli.removedKept: Panel removed (the password and settings are kept).
panel.cli.removedPurged: Panel removed along with its password and settings.
panel.cli.requirePasswordOff: Password in the SSH tunnel: not required.
panel.cli.requirePasswordOn: Password in the SSH tunnel: required.
panel.cli.showHint: The secret part of the address is hidden; in full: kaskadctl panel status --show
panel.cli.siteCert: Let’s Encrypt certificate for {domain}, valid until {date}
panel.cli.statusInactive: The panel is installed but not running (systemctl status {unit}).
panel.cli.statusNotInstalled: The panel is not installed (kaskadctl panel install).
panel.cli.statusPasswordSetTunnel: Password: set (login {login}); required in the tunnel too.
panel.cli.statusPasswordUnsetTunnel: Password: not set; required in the tunnel too.
panel.conf.badDomain: Domain: a name like vpn.example.com (Latin letters, digits, hyphens, dots).
panel.conf.badProxyPath: Panel path: 6–160 characters — Latin letters, digits, “-” and “_”, no “/”.
panel.conf.fixRestart: Fix: restart the panel — systemctl restart kaskad-panel (SSH menu 18).
panel.conf.fixRunDir: Fix: chmod 711 {dir} — or restart the panel (systemctl restart kaskad-panel): it restores the permissions itself.
panel.conf.noExternalAddress: Couldn’t find the server’s external address (ip route get 1.1.1.1 has no src): Access from the internet is unavailable.
panel.conf.noFreePort: Couldn’t find a free port in {lo}–{hi}.
panel.conf.noRunDir: no directory {dir} — the panel is not running
panel.conf.noSocket: no panel socket {sock} — the kaskad-panel service is not listening for nginx
panel.conf.portBusy: Port {port}/tcp is in use: {what}. To take it anyway, use --force.
panel.conf.runDirClosed: directory {dir} isn’t accessible to nginx (mode {mode}, needs traverse permission: 0711)
panel.conf.setPasswordFirst: Set a panel password first — otherwise there is no way to sign in.
panel.conf.socketClosed: panel socket {sock} isn’t accessible to nginx
panel.conf.socketSilent: the panel does not answer on socket {sock} (the kaskad-panel service crashed or is not running)
panel.host.badShare: “Share”: the parameters tariff, country, cpu are 0 or 1 only.
panel.routes.notJson: the request body is not JSON
panel.routes.notJsonObject: the request body is not a JSON object
panel.scheme.accessNew: new protocol {title} — issue its settings to the device (“Users & devices” → “Issue settings”)
panel.scheme.accessRevoked: protocol {title} is revoked: its keys are deleted, the settings on the device will stop working
panel.scheme.accessRevokedLast: ; the device will have no other protocols
panel.scheme.accessRevokedOnline: — the device is online through it now, the connection will drop
panel.scheme.changeSameDevice: {label}: path unchanged — {route}; the route is now pinned to the device
panel.scheme.changeSameUser: {label}: path unchanged — {route}; the route is now pinned to the user
panel.scheme.defaultNoInherit: The default route can’t be “inherited”: choose pool, exit, direct or block.
panel.scheme.diffRemove: {label}: − {title} — its keys and accounts are deleted
panel.scheme.disruptDns: The gateway DNS will restart: for a second or two, site names won’t resolve on any device
panel.scheme.disruptVless: VLESS will reconnect for everyone for a couple of seconds: the gateway’s xray restarts so the device is cut off right away (SOCKS5 and VLESS exits reconnect too)
panel.scheme.disruptXray: The gateway’s xray will restart (a SOCKS5 account added, removed or set to “block”): all connections through SOCKS5, the VLESS protocol and VLESS exits will reconnect
panel.scheme.disruptXrayN: The gateway’s xray will restart (a SOCKS5 account added, removed or set to “block”): all connections through SOCKS5, the VLESS protocol and VLESS exits will reconnect — devices online this way now: {n}
panel.scheme.exitGone: this exit is no longer in the pool — traffic follows the failure policy
panel.scheme.exitNotInPool: Exit {id} isn’t in the “Telegram API proxy” pool — choose another.
panel.scheme.failBad: on exit failure must be block or direct, not {fail}
panel.scheme.forceNote: including YouTube, Telegram, GitHub and Google Play — always, even with a Russian address
panel.scheme.inboundNotInstalled: Protocol {title} isn’t installed on the server — install it in “Protocols” first.
panel.scheme.intentNotObject: Each change must be a JSON object.
panel.scheme.layoutObjects: positions and orders must be JSON objects
panel.scheme.layoutStale: Another tab just saved the diagram layout — loaded it and trying again.
panel.scheme.layoutTooMany: too many blocks in the layout
panel.scheme.layoutVersion: version must be an integer (the layout version this tab has seen)
panel.scheme.leakAlways: “{name}”: now {after} — traffic will go from the server’s address, bypassing exits
panel.scheme.leakFail: “{name}”: now {after} — if the exits go down, traffic will go from the server’s address, bypassing the exit
panel.scheme.noOwnRoute: {label}: has no route of its own anyway — {eff}
panel.scheme.nothingToApply: Nothing to apply: intents must be a non-empty list of changes.
panel.scheme.revokeText: {label}: − protocol {title}{addr}, its keys and accounts are deleted
panel.scheme.routeNeedTarget: route: specify a device, a user or the default.
panel.scheme.rulesNeedTarget: routing rules: specify a device or a user.
panel.scheme.rulesProfileBad: rules profile must be one of: {names}, inherit
panel.scheme.rulesSoon: This version of the Kaskad 3 core doesn’t support routing rules profiles: all traffic follows device routes (“All via exit”).
panel.scheme.stale: Settings changed while you were editing the diagram (another tab, the bot or the menu) — review your changes again.
panel.scheme.stateUnreadable: Can’t read the settings file {path} — open gokaskad in a terminal.
panel.scheme.tooManyIntents: Too many changes at once (more than {max}) — apply them in parts.
panel.scheme.traceInbound: inbound must be one of the device’s inbounds: {kinds}.
panel.scheme.traceNeed: who (device d-…, user u-… or “-”) and target (domain or IPv4 address) are required.
panel.scheme.traceTooLong: String too long — enter a domain or IPv4 address.
panel.scheme.unknownIntent: unknown change {type}: expected grant, revoke, route or rules
panel.scheme.versionString: version must be the string from GET /api/scheme
panel.scheme.warnExitDead: the exit is down right now — until it’s back, traffic goes: {fall}
panel.scheme.warnExitOff: the exit is off for the gateway — until it’s turned on, traffic goes: {fall}
panel.scheme.warnGroupDead: no live exits in the group “{name}” right now — for now traffic goes: {fall}
panel.scheme.warnInboundOff: protocol {title} is off — the device will connect once it’s turned on
panel.scheme.warnKeyBroken: this exit’s key couldn’t be parsed ({problem}) — for now traffic goes: {fall}
panel.scheme.warnLeakDirect: {label}: “direct” route — traffic will go from the server’s address, bypassing exits
panel.scheme.warnLeakFail: {label}: if the exits go down, traffic will go from the server’s address, bypassing the exit — YouTube and Telegram too
panel.scheme.warnNoInboundsLeft: the device will have no protocols left
panel.scheme.warnPanelBlock: the panel is open from this device — after “block” you’ll lose the connection to the panel
panel.scheme.warnPanelInbound: the panel is open from this device through this protocol — you’ll lose the connection to the panel
panel.scheme.warnPoolDead: no live exits in the pool right now — for now traffic goes: {fall}
panel.scheme.warnUnsuited: protocol {title} usually isn’t a good fit for this platform
panel.scheme.whyAny: {via}: any live exit of the pool — picked automatically
panel.scheme.whyEvicted: exit “{name}” is not fit now — through the exit “{to}” of its group
panel.scheme.whyNoAlive: no live exits in the pool — {fall}
panel.scheme.whyVless: pool: one of the VLESS exits — picked automatically
panel.server.badHost: The panel does not answer at this address (Host).
panel.server.badMethod: This method is not allowed here.
panel.server.bodyTooBig: The request body is larger than {mb} MB.
panel.server.noAdminHeader: Request without the X-Kaskad-Admin: 1 header refused (request forgery protection).
panel.server.noCertificate: no server certificate (kaskadctl panel public on creates it)
panel.server.noChunked: Content-Length required: chunked transfer is not supported.
panel.server.notListening: The panel is not listening on {host}:{port}: {why}
panel.speed.err.budget: This test has used up its traffic.
panel.speed.err.busy: Another test is running, in another tab or on another device. Try again a bit later.
panel.speed.err.check: A server check is running — the test will wait for it. Try again a bit later.
panel.speed.err.bytes: The test request size must be a whole number of bytes.
panel.speed.err.day: The daily test limit is reached: {used} of {limit}. Try again tomorrow.
panel.speed.err.expired: The test stopped: time ran out.
panel.speed.err.hour: The hourly test limit is reached: {used} of {limit}. Try again later.
panel.speed.err.lease: Test not found: start it again.
panel.speed.err.store: The test traffic counter could not be saved, so the test did not start.
panel.speed.err.streams: Too many test requests at once.
panel.speed.err.tooBig: The test request is too big.
panel.speed.err.traffic: Tests have used up today’s traffic limit. Try again tomorrow.
panel.speed.log.counterBroken: the counter of browser tests was broken and starts from zero
panel.speed.log.counterUnsaved: the counter of browser tests was not saved: {err}
panel.speed.log.done: browser test: {down} MB down, {up} MB up, {secs} s
panel.speed.log.limits: limits of the browser test in state.json fixed: {notes}
panel.userpage.badAction: action must be enable, rotate or disable
panel.userpage.busy: The server is busy, try again in a few seconds.
panel.userpage.issueFailed: Couldn’t prepare the settings for this protocol.
panel.userpage.locked: The server is applying changes right now, try again in a few seconds.
panel.userpage.notInstalled: The page isn’t installed: no static/user.* files
panel.userpage.noteClosed: The panel is closed to the internet right now (SSH tunnel only), so the user can’t open this link. Turn on “Access from the internet” (SSH menu “Web panel” or the panel’s Settings) — and the link will be complete.
panel.userpage.noteNoHost: The client address isn’t set: kaskadctl gw host <address or name> — without it the link has no address.
panel.userpage.noteNoQr: The server has no qrencode — the page won’t show QR codes (links and files remain). Install it: apt-get install qrencode
panel.userpage.noteSubEmpty: The subscription is empty right now: the user has no enabled devices with VLESS, Hysteria2, AmneziaWG or WireGuard. Grant one of them to a device — the key will appear in the app on the next refresh.
panel.userpage.noteSubPaused: The user is paused: the subscription returns an empty list until access is resumed.
panel.userpage.postOnly: Settings are issued only when you tap the button on the page.
panel.userpage.stale: The page is out of date: reload it and tap the button again.
panel.userpageCli.helpOff: turn the page off: the link stops opening
panel.userpageCli.helpOn: turn the page on and show the link
panel.userpageCli.helpPage: personal page: a secret link with the settings of the user’s devices
panel.userpageCli.helpRotate: new link (the old one stops opening)
panel.userpageCli.helpSub: subscription for apps: its own secret link, the keys of all devices (VLESS, Hysteria2, AmneziaWG, WireGuard)
panel.userpageCli.helpSubList: who has the subscription on (no links)
panel.userpageCli.helpSubOff: revoke the subscription: the link stops working
panel.userpageCli.helpSubOn: turn the subscription on and show the link
panel.userpageCli.helpSubRotate: new subscription link (the old one stops working)
panel.userpageCli.helpUrls: show the links too (they contain the secret)
panel.userpageCli.pageNotOn: “{name}” has no personal page on: kaskadctl page on {ref}
panel.userpageCli.pageOff: Personal page for “{name}” is off: the link no longer opens.
panel.userpageCli.pageRotated: A new link was made for “{name}”; the old one no longer opens.
panel.userpageCli.pageWasOff: “{name}” had no personal page on anyway.
panel.userpageCli.subHowto: Add the link to the app as a subscription: v2RayTun, Hiddify, v2rayN, Streisand and incy take VLESS and Hysteria2, incy on a phone takes AmneziaWG and WireGuard too. Tap “+” and import the link from the clipboard. Refreshes every {hours} h.
panel.userpageCli.subListEmpty: No subscriptions: kaskadctl page sub on <user>
panel.userpageCli.subNotOn: “{name}” has no subscription on: kaskadctl page sub on {ref}
panel.userpageCli.subOff: Subscription for “{name}” revoked: the app will no longer get keys from it.
panel.userpageCli.subRotated: A new subscription link was made for “{name}”; the old one no longer refreshes — add the new one to the app.
panel.userpageCli.subRowPaused: {name}  {user}  subscription on, devices in it: {n} (user disabled)
panel.host.badDay: No such day in the 30-day strip: the date is YYYY-MM-DD, not later than today.
panel.bench.tooBig: The request is too large: at most {max} KB.
panel.bench.speedTest: A test from your device to the server is running, so the server check waits for it. Try again in {s} s.
panel.bench.needEtag: Unknown version of the schedule you are changing — reload the page.
panel.host.badTariff: Plan: a wrong request (values — an object, clear — a list of fields, rev — a string, dry — true or false).
panel.host.badDevRule: The ▲/▼ threshold: pct is a whole percent from {lo} to {hi}, and the request has no other fields.
panel.host.devRuleTooBig: The request is too big: the ▲/▼ threshold is one number, pct.
panel.scheme.ruDefault: by default: direct from the server
panel.scheme.ruNeedTarget: ru_via: specify a device or a user.
panel.scheme.ruNotActing: {label}: the choice is kept, but a domestic group works only with the “Russian sites direct” profile
panel.api.badIps: «ips» — a list of addresses of the server (64 at most).
